title: Compressor pressure buildup — near-miss report
text: On 2024-07-27, compressor CMP-1 at Building 3, Line 2 experienced an overpressure event when the discharge pressure exceeded the safety relief valve (SRV) setpoint of 161 PSI. The SRV opened correctly and vented the excess pressure to the atmosphere. Investigation found that the unloader valve had stuck in the loaded position due to a failed solenoid, causing the compressor to continue building pressure past the normal cutoff. The incident was classified as high severity. Medical treatment beyond first aid was required and/or significant equipment damage occurred. The area was shut down pending investigation.

title: Maintenance Report — Overheating involving induction motor
text: On 2025-09-13, shift supervisor reported smoke emanating from induction motor M-01 in Building 4, Maintenance Bay. Thermal imaging confirmed surface temperature of 110°C, well above the rated maximum of 80°C. Emergency shutdown was initiated per protocol SOP-EM-004. Investigation revealed a seized cooling fan and accumulated dust on the motor housing restricting heat dissipation. The incident was classified as medium severity. Minor first-aid level treatment was required. Equipment was taken out of service for repairs lasting under 24 hours.

title: Accident: Forklift spill event

title: Accident: Crushing hazard at forklift station
text: On 2024-01-27 at approximately 02:00, forklift FLT-12 struck a pedestrian worker in Warehouse A, Loading Dock. The area lacked operational proximity sensors or audible reverse alarms on the forklift. The incident was classified as low severity. No injuries or significant equipment damage occurred. Corrective actions were implemented within the shift.

title: Near-Miss Report — Fire involving conveyor belt
text: A fire was detected on conveyor CB-115 in Building 1, Line 1 on 2023-06-12 at 01:00. The fire originated at a stuck idler roller where friction had ignited accumulated coal dust and rubber debris. The fire suppression system activated within 14 seconds. The fire was contained to a 2-meter section of the belt. No injuries were reported, but production was halted for 5 hours. Investigation found that the dust cleanup schedule had not been followed for 4 weeks. The incident was classified as high severity. Medical treatment beyond first aid was required and/or significant equipment damage occurred. The area was shut down pending investigation.

title: Accident: Conveyor Belt fall event
text: On 2024-12-14, a maintenance technician slipped and fell from the elevated conveyor walkway at Building 1, Line 2 while inspecting belt CB-107. The worker fell approximately 2.0 meters to the lower level. The walkway grating was found to be contaminated with spilled material and lubricant. The worker was wearing appropriate PPE including a hard hat, but was not clipped into the fall arrest system at the time of the incident. The incident was classified as high severity. Medical treatment beyond first aid was required and/or significant equipment damage occurred. The area was shut down pending investigation.

title: Near-Miss: Crushing hazard at forklift station
text: On 2024-12-26 at approximately 18:00, forklift FLT-8 struck a pedestrian worker in Building 4, Maintenance Bay. The forklift operator was reversing with an obstructed rear view due to a loaded pallet stacked above eye level. The pedestrian was walking in a designated forklift aisle without a high-visibility vest. The worker sustained a leg injury from being pinned against a storage rack. The area lacked operational proximity sensors or audible reverse alarms on the forklift. The incident was classified as low severity. No injuries or significant equipment damage occurred. Corrective actions were implemented within the shift.

title: Conveyor Belt fire — near-miss report
text: A fire was detected on conveyor CB-110 in Warehouse B, Storage Area on 2023-10-09 at 04:15. The fire originated at a stuck idler roller where friction had ignited accumulated coal dust and rubber debris. The fire suppression system activated within 18 seconds. The fire was contained to a 1-meter section of the belt. No injuries were reported, but production was halted for 34 hours. Equipment was taken out of service for repairs lasting under 24 hours.

title: Induction Motor mechanical failure — near-miss report
text: Induction motor M-05 in Building 3, Line 1 suffered catastrophic bearing failure on 2023-11-12 at approximately 20:00. The motor had been in continuous service for 7379 hours since last scheduled maintenance. Vibration analysis data from the preceding week showed a progressive increase in amplitude at the bearing defect frequency. The outer race of the drive-end bearing was found fractured. Production on Line 4 was halted for 19 hours during replacement. The incident was classified as CRITICAL severity. Serious injury occurred and/or equipment was destroyed. A full root-cause investigation was mandated by management. Regulatory notification was initiated.

title: Maintenance: Fire hazard at conveyor belt station
text: A fire was detected on conveyor CB-103 in Warehouse A, Loading Dock on 2025-08-23 at 04:15. The fire originated at a stuck idler roller where friction had ignited accumulated coal dust and rubber debris. The fire suppression system activated within 8 seconds. The fire was contained to a 2-meter section of the belt. No injuries were reported, but production was halted for 46 hours. title: Induction Motor mechanical failure — accident report
text: On 2025-01-20, motor M-05 at Building 1, Line 1 experienced a shaft coupling failure during peak production. The flexible coupling element disintegrated, causing the motor to run unloaded at elevated speed before the overload relay tripped after 7 seconds. The root cause was fatigue cracking in the coupling hub, exacerbated by persistent misalignment that had been noted but not corrected in the previous two maintenance inspections. The incident was classified as CRITICAL severity. Serious injury occurred and/or equipment was destroyed. A full root-cause investigation was mandated by management. Regulatory notification was initiated.

title: Accident: Crushing hazard at hydraulic press station
text: On 2025-02-18, an operator at hydraulic press HP-8 in Warehouse A, Loading Dock had their hand caught in the die area when the light curtain safety system failed to detect the intrusion. The operator was reaching to reposition a workpiece that had shifted during the previous cycle. The two-hand control had been bypassed with a zip tie, defeating the safety interlock. The operator sustained crush injuries to two fingers. The incident was classified as medium severity. Minor first-aid level treatment was required. Equipment was taken out of service for repairs lasting under 24 hours.

title: Maintenance: Fire hazard at conveyor belt station
text: A fire was detected on conveyor CB-119 in Building 2, Line 3 on 2024-10-19 at 12:15. title: Maintenance: Electrical Panel fire event
text: A fire was reported in electrical panel EP-6 at Building 1, Line 1 on 2023-10-09 at 22:30. The fire was caused by a loose connection on the main bus bar, which had been generating excessive heat over an extended period. Thermal discoloration and pitting were observed on adjacent conductors. The building's CO2 fire suppression system activated, extinguishing the fire within 14 seconds. Power to the affected section was interrupted for 29 hours during repair. The incident was classified as low severity. No injuries or significant equipment damage occurred. Corrective actions were implemented within the shift.

title: Accident: Fire hazard at electrical panel station

title: Compressor overheating — accident report
text: Compressor CMP-6 at Building 3, Line 2 overheated on 2025-08-24 after the oil cooling system malfunctioned. The discharge air temperature reached 137°C, triggering a high-temperature shutdown. The oil cooler was found to be severely fouled with particulate buildup, reducing cooling capacity by approximately 59%. Additionally, the oil level was found to be 0.7 liters below the minimum mark, suggesting a slow leak at the shaft seal. The incident was classified as high severity. Medical treatment beyond first aid was required and/or significant equipment damage occurred. The area was shut down pending investigation.

Injuries are coded using the Occupational Injury and Illness Classification System. You can apply filters below to view the data according to the filters that were selected. You can download the entire SIR dataset by selecting the "Download the full SIR data set" button at the top of the page, or by selecting filters of your choice, and selecting the "Download Selected Data" button below the chart. These data will be updated periodically and represent incidents under federal OSHA jurisdiction only. They do not include incidents under state plan state jurisdiction. The Severe Injury Report dashboard does not include work-related fatalities. To view work-related fatalities, visitwww.osha.gov/fatalities.
